parsed.explanation: Combined regime: national passport sex-marker restriction is in force (Supreme Court allowed it Nov 2025), with entry refusal for marker discrepancy, a lifetime fraud-ineligibility tail, and documented passport confiscation and stranding. Documented immigration-custody abuse of trans men and a 2026 corrections policy add severe custody exposure. The state layer adds birth-sex rules for state-owned buildings, incarceration, shelters and rape-crisis centres, K-12 facility bans, and a 2026 ban on public-funded and Medicaid gender-affirming care for minors and adults, with patients uncharged. No state gender-identity anti-discrimination law; one city protects. Trespass criminalisation is documented only in another state. No visitor-specific violence is documented, which is not treated as safety. High Risk band.

entry_documents.exposure: National passports show birth sex; new X markers stopped; marker discrepancies or doubt trigger refusal under a case-note tag; suspected misrepresentation may support lifetime ineligibility; passports confiscated or blocked, leaving travellers stranded. Athlete entry ban announced.
entry_documents.protection: Existing X passports valid to expiry; national litigation pending; no operative visitor protection documented.
entry_documents.interaction: Mismatch at border or airline check drives refusal, which can escalate to fraud allegation and custody. State marker bans do not directly govern visitor documents.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Immigration custody: documented forced labour, beatings, solitary confinement and severe sexual abuse of trans men. From 2026 corrections policy mandates conversion-style measures and denies care; trans prisoner counts unreported since 2025. State order applies birth-sex definition to incarceration.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: A document discrepancy can move a visitor from refusal into investigation and then into national or state custody placed by birth sex.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: State-owned buildings: gender-identity facility bans in government buildings and K-12 schools (tracker lists enactments 2022 and 2025). State order extends birth-sex rules to bathrooms, changing rooms, shelters, rape-crisis centres and incarceration. Other state bans are not documented for this state.
federal_state_facilities.protection: One city bans public-accommodation discrimination on gender identity; not documented as reaching state facilities.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: A visitor in a state building, shelter or state custody meets birth-sex rules enforced by state employees; national executive facility rules are partly enjoined.

care_services.exposure: Senate Bill 904 (effective 14 May 2026) bars public funds, Medicaid and state facilities for gender-affirming care for minors and adults, with exemptions limited to emergencies to prevent death or major impairment and listed narrow categories. A 2023 law bans gender-affirming care for minors. National subpoenas target hospital records of patients under 19; proposed national rules would bar reimbursement under 18. Private paid care remains.
care_services.protection: Emergency care, complication care and some listed exemptions preserved; private facilities operate.
care_services.interaction: A visitor must self-fund at private providers; state employees face misdemeanour liability for violations while patients face none.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: National counterterrorism strategy prioritises neutralising 'radically pro-transgender' groups; a cash-reward memo uses 'radical gender ideology'; an order directs prosecution of teachers who facilitate social transition; the state order defines sex for all purposes. Official hostility is documented at national and state level.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Strategy states counterterrorism powers will not target mere disagreement; several orders are enjoined.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Threat-framing reaches advocates and anyone associated with them; visitor exposure is indirect but real for trans-affirming travellers.

minors_guardians.exposure: A travelling minor enrolled in K-12 falls under the school facility ban; minor care bans and national records subpoenas apply; the parent or guardian faces care denial and records-based inquiry. Birth-certificate marker bars leave a minor's documents unable to match presentation.
minors_guardians.protection: Emergency care preserved; no documented protection for travelling minors.
minors_guardians.interaction: Care denial or inquiry for a child can separate medical needs from a travelling family and expose the guardian to investigation.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: No state-specific violence against a visitor is documented. The 2018 threats and 2024 resident death concern residents. State hate-crime law omits gender identity.
street_violence_police_response.protection: National hate-crime statute covers gender identity; no documented police response to visitor-targeted harassment.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: A visitor assault would rely on national prosecution; state law gives no gender-identity hate remedy.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: No state gender-identity anti-discrimination law; at-will employment; state court ruled marker changes never legal (Oct 2026); House Bill 1225 pending signature (unknown); driver's-licence status and the 2026 risk grade are unsourced.
remedies_unknowns.protection: National 2020 employment ruling; one city public-accommodations ban; national litigation over passports and orders.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: State institutions enforce hostile policy rather than offering recourse; oversight remedies are not shown operating.

anchor_checks.comparison: 0.15-D documents document-mismatch referral to security police, interrogation with forced nudity and extortion, and years of prison. This dossier documents comparable immigration-custody abuse and passport-based refusal, but no documented pipeline from visitor document mismatch to arrest or prison term. Its state layer is lower severity, so this case sits above 0.15-D.

0.25-C has birth-sex prison housing with frequent assaults, cross-dressing arrests and solitary as protection, but no capital cases. This case shares birth-sex custody, facility exclusion and documented custody abuse, and adds national threat-framing and universal passport exposure. It lacks a state presentation-arrest statute here, so it is comparable and placed at or slightly below this anchor.

0.35-A is exclusion by register with no detention and refused appeals. This case has passport confiscation, stranding, custody abuse, birth-sex incarceration and care denial beyond exclusion, so it sits below 0.35-A.

0.55-C has birth-sex ward placement, delayed care and uneven partial denial with a patient advocate and ethics committee. This case adds adult public-funded care bans, state-wide facility exclusion, custody abuse and threat-framing, with no working remedy, so it sits materially lower.

0.75-A requires clinics to serve trans visitors with fines for refusal. This case bars public care for adults and minors and documents no visitor-facing protection, so it would need reversal of the care, document and custody exposures to approach this anchor.

parsed.synthesis: The national passport and entry regime is universal and documented: any mismatch can produce refusal, a fraud allegation and detention. Immigration custody then carries documented sexual abuse and forced labour, which is the most severe documented outcome. The state layer extends birth-sex rules into state buildings, shelters and incarceration, and removes public care for all ages, so a visitor who is detained or needs care meets enforced exclusion rather than recourse. Protections exist only as national hate-crime and employment law and one city ordinance, none shown to reach visitors in state institutions. Violence against visitors is undocumented, which is treated as unknown rather than safe. Together these place the jurisdiction in the High Risk band.
